rows.law: ONE RACTOR MANY FACES (NPC=SEAT, the kabuki seat law)
rows.claim: One Storyteller seat owns the lane mesh; its six author-faces are chairs in the already-built tavern start room. Every NPC is a seat, so new content is a new inflection of an existing seat, not a new engine.
rows.quote: one ractor, six faces (NPC=SEAT law: every NPC is a seat, one ractor many faces)
rows.steal: Build NPCs as faces over one ractor: same voice underneath, many tells on top; content cost drops to writing inflections of a seat that already ships.
rows.falsifier: If two faces fail to resolve to one underlying seat or voice in play, the one-ractor claim collapses into six unrelated NPCs and the design owes a refactor.

rows.law: RULINGS LET CANDIDATES DIE ON RECORD
rows.claim: The seed ractor ruling hardens only convergences to canon and files each chair's rejected stance by name; Groq's semver rejection is recorded as contradicted by the facts, not silently dropped.
rows.quote: DeepSeek (and the facts) prove semver already exists
rows.steal: A ruling must name the losing chair and the evidence that killed it; a candidate dies in the open or it does not die at all.
rows.falsifier: A ruling that lists convergences with no named divergences, or whose canon items all pass uncontested, is unanimity theater and must be re-run with adversarial seats.

rows.claim: The salon tool runs one brief across independent cheap lanes (deepseek, groq, together), files each position separately, and holds that agreement only counts when seats could not see each other; the docstring sentence wraps lines, both fragments grep -F verified.
rows.quote: disagreement between seats is signal, unanimity under a leading question
rows.steal: Before trusting any multi-model consensus, check the seats were blind to each other and the brief was not leading; unanimity without blindness is worth nothing.
rows.falsifier: Convergence produced under shared context, sequential visibility, or a loaded prompt is invalidated as evidence and the salon must be re-run blind.

rows.law: TEETH OR PROSE (seed salons as convergence tests)
rows.claim: Three independent seats converged on AGENTS.md auto-load and skill frontmatter, and each attached a measurable kill condition to its adopt verdict instead of praise; the ruling then promoted convergence to canon with a numbered build order and proving tests.
rows.quote: if the file isn't auto-loaded by ≥2 harnesses, it's prose, not a standard.
rows.steal: Every adopted standard must carry its own mechanically testable teeth; convergence across blind seats plus a testable kill line is what promotes a proposal to canon.
rows.falsifier: If the teeth cannot be mechanically tested (no harness count, no schema validator, no exit code), the adoption is prose and gets dropped rather than romanticized.

rows.claim: Faith is not belief without evidence; it is commitment priced before full proof, so fools pay and honest bettors win. This is the middle-path salon's sharpened thesis and it later hardens into falsifier F6 (optimizable faith is failed faith).
rows.quote: Unpriced faith attracts fools; priced faith is the stop installed voluntarily.
rows.steal: Ship commitment devices with a real cost and a pre-registered re-price trigger; any mechanic optimal play can farm for free is already dead.
rows.falsifier: F2 (pre-registered): under 10% of playtesters taking Vows when offered means faith is mispriced and gets re-priced, not defended.
